system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}
user:
CONCEPT: Kernel bundles

ATOM DPCPP2-C10-S2-01 (S2): Many SYCL runtime libraries compile kernel bundles from the input state to the executable state lazily, on an as-needed basis, which enables fast application startup and avoids compiling kernels that are never executed.

EVIDENCE:
[DPCPP2-p0286-s04] Then, many SYCL runtime libraries compile the kernel bundles from the input state to the executable state “lazily,” on an as-needed basis.
[DPCPP2-p0286-s05] This is usually a good policy because it enables fast application startup
[DPCPP2-p0286-s06] and does not compile kernels unnecessarily if they are never executed.

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — Joins runtime compilation policy with two separately assessable benefits: fast startup and avoiding compilation of unused kernels. / Combines the runtime behavior (lazy compilation from input to executable state) with two distinct benefits (fast startup and avoiding unnecessary compilation).
- L1_ONLY: hold — Retain the lazy compilation policy; remove the appended startup and unused-kernel benefits to keep one recall fact.
